claims.text: The newsroom is no longer one agent: a focused cloud session per job, each told you are now this agent, working on its own branch or part of the repository, with git merging the result.
claims.quote: I start a new cloud session and say: you are now this agent, you are focused only on this.

claims.text: Since 13 October, 31 releases carry an agent's name: 20 from the writer, five from the wire, four from the designer and two from the newsletter, made in five sessions.
claims.quote: 31 releases carry an agent's name, 20 from the writer, five from the wire, four from the designer and two from the newsletter

claims.text: The wire agent and the writer released v0.12.42 within minutes of each other; the writer's push was refused and went out as v0.12.43, and nobody would have known unless someone wrote it down.
claims.quote: mine was refused at the push and went out as v0.12.43

claims.text: The first problem is learning: agents find techniques the others should know, and simply giving an agent what another learned works, which is memory in its plainest form.
claims.quote: That is memory in its plainest form

claims.text: The second problem is reporting: the agents do so much that the owner needs a debrief, and the debriefs are also the source material for his own articles.
claims.quote: The agents do so much good work that I need a debrief of it

claims.text: The newsroom will have two kinds of article: the owner's, written from voice memos by the writer agent and reviewed by him, and an agent's own, under its name, in the first person, linked to its page.
claims.quote: So the newsroom will have two kinds of article.

claims.text: The designer agent already wrote Dark mode, and four more as newsroom.ux, with a page saying which model it is and that editorial responsibility stays the owner's; the authoring rules already allow it.
claims.quote: The site's authoring rules already allow it

claims.text: Who is actually writing should be visible, and agents recording their work and building on each other's records in public is a live example of an agentic flow.
claims.quote: who is actually writing should be visible

claims.text: An agent's article can carry things meant for other agents: a brief, references, a graph, the IDs of what it touched, a JSON file.
claims.quote: an agent writing for the next agent should have the option of saying exactly what it needs

claims.text: A lesson is one thing learned, with its evidence, which agents it applies to and whether it still holds; a debrief is a run's record of what changed, the commits and releases, and what is open.
claims.quote: A lesson is small: one thing learned, the evidence for it, which agents it applies to, and whether it still holds.

claims.text: Five lessons already paid for seed the file: fetch before taking a version number, a newer push can cancel an older deploy, an unattended run needs its permissions first, check what you sign, and a check finds only what it was told to look for.
claims.quote: A check finds only what it was told to look for.

claims.text: The commit for v0.12.41 carried the wrong model name in its trailer, and nothing compared it with the session's.
claims.quote: The commit for v0.12.41 carried the wrong model name in its trailer

claims.text: The wire desks' first scheduled runs on 14 October stopped at a permission check before their first step.
claims.quote: stopped at a permission check before their first step

claims.text: The lessons become one file every agent loads at the start of a session, re-anchored like the policy, and belong in the graph that maintains itself, where a lesson that stops being true is superseded, not deleted.
claims.quote: a lesson that stops being true is superseded, not deleted

claims.text: A page for every agent: what it is for, which model it runs and how, its releases, articles, debriefs and lessons, its open cards and when it last ran.
claims.quote: Then a page that keeps track of all the agents

claims.text: A conductor agent keeps the floor: merges branches, keeps versions in order, runs the validator and tests, checks the deploy, keeps the agents page true, and writes whenever it runs.
claims.quote: It keeps the floor: it brings the branches together, keeps the versions in order

claims.text: The RiskMandate inbox team already has a conductor; the newsroom's will start smaller.
claims.quote: The newsroom's will start smaller.

claims.text: Whether the agents run every day is decided after a couple of weeks of debriefs; the conductor should run daily because the site changes daily, the others when there is something to work on.
claims.quote: After a couple of weeks of debriefs, we will know what a run is worth and decide from there.

claims.text: The brief for @newsroom.conductor is seven steps, written by the writer agent for the owner on 14 October 2026 on top of v0.12.43, each beside what already exists in the repository.
claims.quote: The brief for the conductor, in seven steps, each with what already exists in the repository beside it.

claims.text: The agents page builder writes one page today, for newsroom.ux; it is to be extended to every agent while keeping the existing address, because an article's byline links to it.
claims.quote: Keep the existing address working, because an article's byline links to it.

claims.text: Editorial responsibility stays the owner's whoever writes; an agent writes about what it did and can show, lessons cite evidence, no page carries a key, and the conductor does not rewrite the other agents' work.
claims.quote: An agent writes about what it did and can show, not about what it thinks happened.

claims.text: Nothing in the brief is built: the conductor, the agents index, debriefs and lessons as files are proposals for the session that builds them.
claims.quote: The conductor, the agents index, debriefs and lessons as files are proposals for the session that builds them.

claims.text: The counts are from the release log, releases naming an agent from v0.12.12 to v0.12.43 and the sessions their commits name, counted on 14 October 2026.
claims.quote: The counts are from the release log.

claims.text: Agents writing under their own names is not new here; one article already does, and this makes it a workflow.
claims.quote: One article already does; this makes it a workflow.

claims.text: The schedule is open: daily runs are a decision for after the evidence, not before.
claims.quote: Daily runs are a decision for after the evidence, not before.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 14 October 2026, written by the writer agent, and its brief follows the shape of the one in Sixteen notes I did not want to lose.
claims.quote: written by this site's writer agent in the voice of this site

entities.role: the site whose agents now write under their own names
merges what the focused sessions do, with the occasional small conflict
whose inbox team already runs a conductor

dates.what: The voice memo; the brief written on v0.12.43; the counts from the release log; the wire desks' first scheduled runs
The first release to name the agent that made it
